title: What happens to the mean when 2 is taken from every value?
description: Some number of values have a mean of a, and two is subtracted from every one of them. The board uses letters to find the new sum and the new mean. Keeko's doubt is that the mean falls by two times the number of values.
teaching_notes: One idea: the sum falls by two for each value, so the sum falls by two times n, and dividing by n brings the fall in the mean down to two. Watch for students who say the mean falls by the same amount as the sum.

source: Use algebra to show what happens to the mean when 2 is subtr
video_script.why: The child proves with letters that taking the same number from every value takes that number from the mean.
video_script.substitution: Call the values x1 to xn and the mean a, write the new sum, collect the twos, and divide by n.
video_script.anchor: a row of values x1, x2 up to xn with their mean a written below, and a minus 2 arrow over every value
video_script.wrong_answer: the mean falls by two times en
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the mean falls by two times n. The sum falls by two times n, but the mean is the sum divided by n, so the mean falls by only two.
video_script.payoff_line: The new mean is eigh minus two

final_answer.spoken: the new mean is eigh minus two

hold_back: Answer: The new mean is a − 2
never_show: the final answer line before the answer beat
maths_rules: values x1, x2, ..., xn with (x1 + x2 + ... + xn) / n = a
new mean = (x1 + x2 + ... + xn - 2n) / n = a - 2
Keeko's doubt: the sum falls by 2n, but the mean falls by 2n / n = 2
video_script.design: One idea: taking two from every value takes two from the mean. The row of letters stays from ground to the end of the idea part. Wrong idea: the mean falls by two times n.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a row of values x1, x2, ..., xn with the mean a written below; an arrow labelled every value minus 2; a box with a question mark

marks.book: the title card From your book appears
marks.row: a row of values x1, x2 and so on up to xn appears, with the mean a written below
marks.ask: an arrow labelled every value minus 2 appears, and a box with a question mark sits beside the mean

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the mean of any number of values.
<bookmark mark='row'/>There are en values, ex one, ex two and so on up to ex en. Their mean is eigh.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>If two is taken from every value, what happens to the mean?

beats.on_screen: the row of values and the question box stay; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board while the row stays in view

beats.on_screen: labels under the row: n = how many values; a = the mean; x1 to xn = the values

marks.letters: labels appear under the row: n for how many values, a for the mean, x1 to xn for the values
marks.twos: a small minus 2 appears under each of the values, one for each value

narration: <bookmark mark='letters'/>The letter en stands for how many values there are, and eigh stands for their mean.
<bookmark mark='twos'/>Taking two from every value means taking two away en times.

beats.on_screen: Given: values x1, x2, …, xn with (x1 + x2 + … + xn) ÷ n = a

marks.given: the values and the rule for their mean are written as the given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, en values whose sum divided by en is eigh.

beats.on_screen: To find: the new mean when 2 is subtracted from every value

marks.find: the thing to find is written under the given

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the new mean when two is taken from every value.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Step one, the new sum. Take two from ex one, take two from ex two, and go on up to ex en.

marks.collect: the twos are gathered into one block: x1 + x2 + … + xn − 2n

beats.moves_through: the twos slide together into one block
narration: <bookmark mark='collect'/>Step two, collect the twos. There are en twos in all, so the new sum is the old sum minus two en.

beats.on_screen: new mean = (x1 + x2 + … + xn − 2n) ÷ n = a − 2

marks.divide: the new sum is divided by n, giving the old mean a and then 2n ÷ n = 2

narration: <bookmark mark='divide'/>Step three, divide by en. The old sum divided by en is eigh, and two en divided by en is two.
<bookmark mark='result'/>We are left with eigh minus two.

beats.on_screen: Answer: The new mean is a − 2
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The new mean is eigh minus two.
Taking two from every value takes two from the mean.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the row of values
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a bubble saying the mean falls by 2n; the sum falls by 2n and 2n ÷ n = 2 shown beside it; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble says the mean falls by 2n
marks.fix: the fall of 2n is marked on the sum, and 2n ÷ n = 2 is written for the mean
marks.rule: the bubble is struck through and a − 2 is circled

beats.colours: warning colour for the struck bubble
narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the mean falls by two times en.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The fall of two en belongs to the sum. The mean is the sum divided by en, so its fall is two en divided by en.
